question: Which of the following languages has maximum number of speakers in India according to the Census 2011 data?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bengali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bengali is the second most spoken language in India according to the Census 2011 data, following Hindi.
 
• There are approximately 83 million Bengali speakers in India as per Census 2011.
 
• Bengali is predominantly spoken in the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura, and Assam.
 
• The language has a rich literary heritage and is one of the 22 scheduled languages of India recognized by the Indian Constitution.
 
• Bengali is also the official language of the state of West Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindi:**

 
 
• Hindi is the most spoken language in India with over 528 million speakers according to Census 2011.
 
• It is the official language of the central government of India.
 
• Hindi is written in the Devanagari script and has a rich tradition of literature and poetry.
 
 
 
• **Languages of India:**
 
 
• India is a multilingual country with 22 officially recognized languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These languages include Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• The Census 2011 is the 15th National Census of India conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India.
 
• It provides detailed information about the population, economic activity, literacy, housing, and amenities, among other demographic data.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit:**
 
 
• Sanskrit is an ancient language of India and is known as the mother of many Indian languages.
 
• It is used extensively in classical Indian literature, philosophy, and religious texts.
 
• Though not widely spoken, it holds significant cultural and historical importance.
